question: True or false: in a century of South American internationals, high-altitude home sides won no more often than low-lying ones?
answer: False. McSharry analysed 1,460 matches from 1900 to 2004: between teams from the same altitude, the home side won about 54% of the time; with a gap of about 3,700 m, like La Paz over the coast, about 83%. Each extra 1,000 m of difference added about half a goal to the home margin.
move: Before crediting the crowd, check what else the home ground supplies.
ask: When I do better on my own turf, how much is the place itself doing the work?
trap: Treating home advantage as crowd support, the same at every ground.
reference: Patrick E. McSharry, Effect of altitude on physiological performance: a statistical analysis using results of international football games, BMJ, 2007
